72  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

"Well, judge Guilford Webb, in Savoy College 'Ex-Students' Business Meeting, September 5, 1935, said, five years later my conversation with President Halbell would never permit a student to break off the bills, handled them five hundred dollars in bills, and made those bills to be looked for in a way."⁵² Ex-students believe that President Halbell would never stop to inquire if a student could help the situation by taking care of the bill itself, while pointing out to the astonished student the amount of money left, sometimes it was as much as fifty or a hundred dollars each time.

In handling the maintenance expenses of the institution, Mr. Halbell showed a remarkable ingenuity. Information is not available as to how the teachers and assistants for the Primary and Commercial departments received their pay. From those fees it must have been clear that some if not all of them did part-time teaching while cutting toward their salaries; and in those early days far from the college expenses were part, at least, of the compensation. In addition, President Halbell, through the work of Silvaus Female Institute in Virginia, the South Kentucky at Hopkinsville, and the Southeastern State, the numbered teachers were ministers, there was never any attempt to enhance the instruction because some were ministers.

The "whole-house" keeping of the dormitory was apparently done largely by student labor, and the students who worked their board were employed for this purpose. The older students did part of the farming on the College farm, and some interruptions due to illness he had spent the early twenty-eight years as teacher, from Silvaus Female Institute in Virginia, the South Kentucky at Hopkinsville, and the Southeastern State.

⁵²Guilford Webb, in Savoy College 'Ex-Students' Business Meeting, Savoy, Texas, August 5, 1935.
